en: Warm ocean water evaporates, creating low pressure that pulls in surrounding air to spin into a typhoon.
Magma cools slowly underground to form intrusive igneous rock like granite, creating large visible mineral crystals.
Earth blocks direct sunlight from reaching the Moon during a lunar eclipse, casting a dark shadow on it.
Water vapor cools high in the atmosphere and condenses around dust particles to form clouds that release rain.
Acid rain weathers limestone rocks by dissolving their calcium carbonate, gradually breaking them down to form soil.
Solar gravity pulls Earth inward while its forward motion keeps the planet moving in a curved orbit.
A massive star exhausts its nuclear fuel and collapses under its own gravity, triggering a supernova explosion.
The warm Gulf Stream current carries tropical heat northward, making the climate of Western Europe much milder.
Rising magma builds immense pressure inside Mount Pinatubo until it explosively erupts, releasing massive ash clouds upward.
Intense underground heat and pressure squeeze and bake shale, transforming it into the metamorphic rock called slate.
Land heats faster than the ocean during the day, causing cooler sea air to rush inland as a breeze.
Lunar gravitational pull draws ocean water toward the Moon, creating a high tide bulge on the surface.
